Senses.PreferredTarget: gaze freely and trace the tracks of flying birds
SearchAliases: look broadly and write out the traces of flying birds
gaze at will and draw forth the tracks of flying birds
Senses.Explanation: 縱觀寫出飛禽跡 means gaze freely and trace the tracks of flying birds. A reusable poetic line in which an unrestricted or sweeping gaze writes out the tracks of birds in flight. Its paired line likewise makes slow walking break the sound of flowing water. Zen masters reuse the line as a capping response or image of conduct that cannot be reduced to an ordinary visible trail.
Senses.Note: Retain the impossible-track image. The sources do not establish a single doctrinal paraphrase such as enlightenment, freedom, or emptiness. Do not silently expand this headword to the whole two-line couplet.
